title: lore emits no contractVersion; quest does -- ruled conformant, additive whenever lore wants it
description:
FILED AS A RULING ALREADY MADE, NOT AS A DEFECT TO FIX. Read this before re-opening it.

THE FACT, measured on 2026-09-15 immediately before the v0.7.0 tag. quest 0.7.0 carries a top-level
`contractVersion` (a global integer, distinct from `schemaVersion`) on its SUCCESS envelopes. lore
0.7.0 carries it nowhere -- zero occurrences across src/, test/ and docs/. So a consumer writing
`if ('contractVersion' in envelope)` gets a different answer per CLI at the same version 0.7.0.

  lore 0.7.0 success  [schemaVersion, kind, data, principal]
  lore 0.7.0 error    [error_type, message, hint, input, principal]
  quest 0.7.0 success [schemaVersion, contractVersion, kind, data, principal]
  quest 0.7.0 error   [error_type, message, principal]

HOW IT WAS MEASURED MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE RESULT. The `lore` on PATH resolves to 0.6.2, so reading
it would have answered confidently about the wrong release. Both repos ran their OWN 0.7.0 artifact
instead -- lore via `bun run src/cli.ts` (self-reports 0.7.0), quest by extracting the binary from
its tag and running it from a scratch path. That discipline is the only reason the answer means
anything.

=== IT IS CONFORMANT. BOTH OF THEM. DO NOT RE-OPEN THIS AS AN ASYMMETRY TO REMEDY. ===

ODOC-195 (opum-doc PR #274, merged 2026-09-15T09:05:55Z at 2f69e075, BEFORE either 0.7.0 tag)
ratifies that an envelope's top-level key set is OPEN to addition on both success and error
envelopes, that a consumer MUST tolerate an unrecognised top-level key, and that ratification applies
only to identity-bearing keys. It then names quest's field explicitly, at
docs/specs/opum-command-contract.md:558 -- ordinary additive version-signal metadata, not an identity
assertion, named there so lore-cli, which shares this envelope shape, has the same visibility into it.

Read at that line on opum-doc main directly, NOT taken from the orchestrator's relay of it. The relay
was accurate; the rule is that a record is read rather than received, and it was applied here.

SO: lore omitting it at 0.7.0 is correct, quest carrying it is correct, and lore may add it
unilaterally whenever it wants under the permitted-addition bullet. Retraction, once shipped, would
be the breaking change -- so adding it is a one-way door and deserves a reason, not just symmetry.

=== THE CONSTRAINT THAT ACTUALLY BINDS, if lore ever does add it ===

contractVersion must NOT go on the ERROR envelope. opum-cli-e2e's shared check (lib/check.mjs:189,
backing both 10-contract-quest.mjs and 11-contract-lore.mjs) allow-lists the NAMED SET
{error_type, message, hint, input, principal}, with hint and input optional. lore's five keys ARE
that set; quest's three are a subset; both conform today and nothing is red. An unrecognised key
reddens the row for whichever CLI adds it -- identically. That, not any quest-specific accommodation,
is the real reason behind QCLI-289's success-envelope-only decision.

I raised lore's extra hint/input as a possible trip of that allow-list; quest-cli disposed of it by
reading the consumer's code rather than either of us assuming. Recorded because the wrong version of
this ("quest's envelope is a closed three") was in circulation and is narrower than the truth.

THAT ALLOW-LIST IS ITSELF OUT OF CONFORMANCE with ODOC-195 as amended, since it rejects an
unrecognised top-level key the Spec says a consumer MUST tolerate. Already filed as opum-cli-e2e
TASK-66 and deliberately held behind baselines/v0.7.0-pair so the pair diff isolates product changes
from harness ones. NOT lore's to chase, and relaxing a harness constraint inside the window where the
harness is qualifying the release would be the wrong move anyway.

acceptanceCriteria.text: If lore adds contractVersion, it goes on the SUCCESS envelope only -- never the error envelope, which would redden opum-cli-e2e rows until their TASK-66 lands
Any decision to add it cites a reason beyond symmetry with quest, since a shipped top-level key can only be retracted via a breaking change
This task is closed as wont-do rather than left open indefinitely if lore decides omission is the permanent answer
